newsitem.title: POLAND: Savings seen key to Poland's growth, EU accession.
newsitem.headline: Savings seen key to Poland's growth, EU accession.

text.p: Poland needs to increase the level of savings to ensure long-term, fast economic growth which is pivotal for the country to meet European Union accession criteria, the World Bank said in a report.

"A quickly growing economy is one of the most certain signs that Poland is able to meet the challenges of EU membership," the summary of the World Bank's Country Economic Report, to be published in full later this year, said.
"The primary condition for the realisation of the growth strategy is to increase the level of domestic savings," it said.
Poland has become an associate member of the EU in 1994 and expects to become a full member shortly after the year 2000.

The report, distributed to journalists, said the main way to cut state spending, encourage savings and curb inflation was to reform the inefficient pension system, restructure loss-making state-owned firms and speeding up privatisation.
The government's scheme of reforming the pension system was "prepared well," the report said.

It also stressed the need for Poland to continue the liberalisation of its trade policies and foreign investment regulations as well as strengthening the legal framework for the operation of the booming private sector.
The report said that before Poland became an EU member it would have to liberalise the energy, telecommunications, transport and financial sectors.

It said the restructuring of the coal, steel and chemical sectors as well as of cooperative banks, the State Savings Bank PKO BP and the state-owned insurance firm PZU SA was necessary even though it was not a direct condition for the EU entry.

"Without faster privatisation state-owned companies and banks will find it increasingly difficult to compete on the European market and will become a potential source of fiscal problems and unemployment," the report said.

It said Poland would also have to tackle some problems, such as environmental protection, over a longer time, but stressed that, especially in the case of air pollution, the benefits from implementing EU standards would be much higher than costs.
The report said Poland's agriculture policies should aim to support farmers' incomes and not focus on price interventions.

"Poland's agriculture policy goals should be to strengthen market institutions, reduced and more transparent interventions on the grain market and implementation of EU technical and quality standards," it said.

The report also said Poland would be able to solve its unemployment problem if it supported the mobility of the workforce through housing programmes and its qualification through an overhaul of the education system.
